candidate.blueprint_locator: Safe and Effective Care Environment — Management of Care; coordinate referrals and collaborate with interprofessional team members based on client needs
candidate.blueprint_topic: Management of Care — individualized specialty referral in diabetes
candidate.educational_objective: Coordinate diabetes specialty referrals according to the client’s actual complications, comorbidities, treatment complexity, and support needs rather than applying a universal referral rule or laboratory cutoff.

options.A: Arrange referrals according to the client’s complications, comorbidities, treatment complexity, and individual needs rather than assuming every client with diabetes requires the same specialist.
options.B: Refer every adult with diabetes to endocrinology at diagnosis because specialty care is universally required regardless of clinical needs.
options.C: Use a single hemoglobin A1C value as a universal rule that automatically determines whether endocrinology referral is required.
options.D: Avoid specialty referral once diabetes is diagnosed because primary care alone should manage all diabetes-related complications.

candidate.rationale: A is correct. The 2026 ADA Standards of Care emphasize individualized, team-based diabetes care and recommend specialist referrals as appropriate for complications, comorbidities, treatment burden, and other person-specific needs. The standards do not establish one universal endocrinology referral threshold for every adult with type 2 diabetes, nor do they require endocrinology referral for every diagnosis. B and C impose unsupported universal rules. D is incorrect because diabetes-related complications often require collaboration with appropriate specialists such as endocrinology, nephrology, cardiology, ophthalmology, podiatry, behavioral health, or other professionals depending on the clinical problem.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Current ADA standards support individualized specialist referral based on complications, comorbidities, treatment burden, and client needs rather than a universal endocrinology referral requirement or single A1C cutoff.
candidate.source_document_title: Improving Care and Promoting Health in Populations: Standards of Care in Diabetes—2026; Comprehensive Medical Evaluation and Assessment of Comorbidities: Standards of Care in Diabetes—2026
